d6f3d52f2671: Salesforce appointment scheduling with no code: offer only the times you choose, set times per advisor, keep clients private, and let them book on your site.
145db718fdf6: How do I schedule appointments in Salesforce without code?
4aa1c4a31bd3: Add the MultiDatePick Resource Booking calendar to a record page, an app page, a Screen Flow or an Experience Cloud site, and point it at your own appointment object and your advisors. Then choose the start times you offer, the appointment length, minimum notice, limits per client and closed days in the Setup Wizard. Staff book inside Salesforce, clients book on your site, and every appointment is a record on your own object.
2a10c371a8ed: Can I offer only set appointment times, like 9:00 and 10:30?
d94d8aabf46f: Yes. Choose Only these times in the Setup Wizard and add each start time, for example 9:00, 10:30, 1:00, 2:30 and 4:00. The time grid shows only those starts, each lasting the Booking Length. A listed time that is taken, closed or too soon shows greyed out.
416a57b61db1: Can each advisor have their own appointment times?
20f95decaba1: Yes. Add a text field to your advisor object, type each advisor's start times in 24-hour form, such as 08:00,09:30,11:00, and set Only These Times Field to it. When a client picks that advisor, the grid shows that advisor's times. Each advisor's working hours can come from two time fields on their record too.
2d6404909411: Can clients book appointments on an Experience Cloud site without logging in?
acb82bc3886b: Yes. The calendar works on public Experience Cloud pages for guests. A pop-up asks for their name, email and other details before the appointment saves, and every limit, notice period and conflict check runs on the server.
23314e100d1b: Can a client see other clients' appointments?
f16f85690d21: Not when you choose Busy. Set Show Other People's Bookings As to Busy for site guests, or Busy for everyone, and other appointments draw as a hatched Unavailable block with no name, no details and no link. The names are removed on the server, so they never reach the browser.
dcb19d60313f: Do I need Salesforce Scheduler to book appointments in Salesforce?
ee7eb6041306: No. Salesforce Scheduler is an add-on license with its own data model. MultiDatePick books appointments on the objects you already have, custom or standard, for $20 per user per month with every feature included. See how the two compare.

eac4373e76c2: List the start times you offer, such as 9:00, 10:30, 1:00, 2:30 and 4:00. The grid shows those and nothing else.
1e5522587951: One text field on the advisor holds their own list. Pick the advisor and the grid follows it.
897a43201094: A 30, 45 or 60 minute appointment books in one click, with a buffer after each one if you want it.
4d1403ec8b3a: Other clients' appointments show as Busy, with no name, no details and no link, enforced on the server.

1e2de049244e: Offer only the appointment times you choose
cbfb2f3bcd01: Most calendars cut the day into equal slots: every 15 or 30 minutes from opening to close. That suits a meeting room. It does not suit a practice that sees clients at 9:00, 10:30, 1:00, 2:30 and 4:00, with the gaps between kept for notes, calls and lunch.
2d59e8a9a7e6: <t1>Only these times</t1> fixes that. In the Setup Wizard, choose Only these times and add each start time. The time grid then offers those starts and no others, on every day and in every view. Each one lasts the <t2>Booking Length</t2>, so a 60 minute length turns 10:30 into a 10:30 to 11:30 appointment in one click.
58e449124af1: Everything else still guards a listed time. A time that is already booked, closed for the day, too soon for your notice period, outside the advisor's hours or too close to the next appointment shows greyed out, so clients see the time exists and is taken, instead of a gap they cannot explain.
b6013267969c: Each advisor, their own times and hours
58feb30bba2b: One advisor works mornings, another sees clients at 8:00 before the office opens, a third keeps Fridays for reviews. Add a text field to your advisor object, such as <t1>Available Times</t1>, and type each advisor's starts in 24-hour form:
b52ee18c6eb5: . Point <t1>Only These Times Field</t1> at it (in the Setup Wizard, <t2>Each Resource's Own Times</t2>), and when a client picks that advisor, the grid shows that advisor's times. An advisor with the field left blank uses the calendar's own list.
429029849615: Working hours come from the advisor too: <t1>Business Hours Start Field</t1> and <t2>Business Hours End Field</t2> read two time fields on the advisor record. A day off, a training afternoon or an office closure goes in your closures object with an optional advisor, so it closes the day for one advisor or for everyone, and can show its reason on the calendar. When one appointment needs two people, such as an advisor and a specialist, only the times both of them offer are shown.
34db4e1509df: Booked by staff in Salesforce, or by clients on your site
64618ef6b5ee: The same calendar works in both places. <t1>Staff</t1> book from a record page, an app page or a Screen Flow, with every detail visible: who is booked, for what, and in what status. <t2>Clients</t2> book on a public Experience Cloud page without logging in. The <t3>Record details pop-up</t3> asks them for their name, email, the meeting type and a note before the appointment saves.
ab4183cb9cb6: On a public site, the client gives their details in a pop-up before the appointment saves.
90c70a83ab36: On that public page, other clients' appointments show as <t1>Busy</t1>. 2708fdde2414: Rules that keep the appointment book sane
6d74c1394709: Each rule is one setting, and each is checked again on the server when the appointment saves, so reloading the page never gets around it.
6f90fb083b35: <t1>Minimum Notice (Hours)</t1>: 24 requires a full day of notice. Earlier days are greyed out, and on the cut-off day the earlier times close.
97a8cf3485bc: <t1>Book Up To (Days Ahead)</t1>: 60 keeps the book open two months out, and moves forward every day.
58396708184f: <t1>Limit per Person</t1>: how many upcoming appointments one client can hold, counted by their email or contact in <t2>Limit per Person Client Field</t2>. Staff can book past it after a confirmation; site visitors cannot.
193e7fb9e519: <t1>Max Bookings per Day</t1>: how many separate appointments one person can pick on a single day.
af5971c88a1e: Holidays, office closures and days off, for the whole office or one advisor, for a whole day or part of one, with the reason shown.
2ae02b4e4856: <t1>Buffer Between Bookings (Minutes)</t1>: 15 keeps a quarter hour free after each appointment.
0663d9ac49f0: A taken time is greyed out before anyone clicks, and the save checks again. <t1>How conflicts and capacity work</t1>.
327972e88116: An appointment moves through a life: requested, confirmed, met, sometimes cancelled or missed. Point <t1>Status Field</t1> at your status picklist and each status gets its own color. <t2>Selectable Statuses</t2> decides what a booking can be saved as: set it to Requested on the public page, and every client request arrives as Requested for your team to confirm. Add Cancelled to <t3>Ignored Statuses</t3>, and a cancelled appointment frees its time at once.
2c270ea5b64d: One advisor's month, colored by status: Requested, Confirmed, Met, No-Show and Cancelled.
4a70b6524d90: The client gets a confirmation the moment they book: turn on <t1>Show In-Component Toast</t1> and write your own words in <t2>Success Toast Message</t2>, such as "Thank you. We will confirm your appointment within one business day."
785d329a2bfc: Reminders and follow-ups with a Flow button
54f7727fb821: The Setup Wizard's custom buttons run one of your own Flows. Put a <t1>Send a reminder</t1> button on every appointment, and staff send the reminder from the calendar in one click. A button can show only on certain statuses, such as Confirmed, act on several appointments picked in Edit Mode, or run on its own after every save, so a Flow can send the confirmation email without anyone pressing anything.
4e8316f4d396: A Send a reminder button on each appointment runs the Flow the admin picked.
